articles.zh: 球员罚点球时，脑子里在想什么
body: Taking a penalty looks simple, but inside a footballer's head it is anything but simple. In those few seconds, the brain has to handle noise, pressure and the fear of failing in front of millions of people.
罚一个点球看着简单，但球员脑子里一点都不简单。就那么几秒钟，大脑要同时应付噪音、压力，还有当着几百万人失手的恐惧。
Researchers who study top players say the best ones are not always the calmest. They are simply the fastest at shutting out distractions, so their attention narrows to the ball and nothing else.
研究顶级球员的学者说，最厉害的那批人不一定是最冷静的，他们只是屏蔽干扰的速度最快——注意力一下就缩到球上，别的什么都不看。
The good news is that this skill can be trained. Breathing slowly, following a fixed routine and picturing the shot before taking it all help ordinary people stay steady under pressure too.
好消息是，这本事是能练的。慢慢呼吸、每次都走同一套固定流程、动手前先在脑子里过一遍——这几招放在普通人身上，同样能让你在压力下稳住。

articles.zh: 我们是不是该多骑骑自行车
body: Cycling is cheap, quiet and good for your heart, so why do so many bikes sit unused in the garage? For most people, the honest answer is traffic.
骑车便宜、安静，还对心脏好，那为什么那么多自行车就搁在车库里落灰？对大多数人来说，实话实说，是因为路上车太多。
Cities that built protected bike lanes saw riders come back within months. Once people feel safe, cycling stops being a sport and simply becomes a way to get to work.
那些修了带隔离的自行车道的城市，几个月内骑车的人就回来了。只要感觉安全，骑车就不再是一项运动，而只是上下班的一种方式。
You do not need special clothes or an expensive bike. A short ride to the shops a few times a week is already enough to improve your mood, your sleep and your fitness.
你不需要专业装备，也不需要贵的车。一周骑几次、去趟超市那么短的距离，就已经足够改善心情、睡眠和体能了。

articles.zh: 为什么你的邮件读起来像在凶人
body: Almost everyone has opened an email that felt cold or sharp. Very often the sender never meant to be rude at all — they were simply in a hurry.
几乎每个人都收到过读着冷冰冰、甚至有点冲的邮件。可很多时候发件人压根没想凶你，他只是当时忙得很。
Without a face or a voice, short sentences can easily sound angry. A missing 'please', a one-word reply, or too many capital letters can change the tone completely.
邮件里没有表情也没有语气，短句子就特别容易被读成生气。少一个 please、只回一个词、大写字母用太多，语气立刻就变了。
A simple fix is to read your message once more before you send it. Adding a greeting, a thank you and one warm line usually solves the whole problem.
解决办法很简单：发出去之前再读一遍。加一句问候、一句谢谢、一句稍微暖一点的话，基本就没事了。

articles.en: Why Are We All So Stressed?
articles.zh: 为什么我们个个都这么累
body: Many people say they feel stressed almost every day. Work, money and the constant flow of news all add weight to a mind that never really switches off.
很多人说自己几乎天天都在焦虑。工作、钱、还有刷不完的新闻，都在往一个从来没真正停下来过的脑子里加码。
A little stress is actually useful, because it helps us meet deadlines. The trouble starts when the body stays alert for weeks, which affects sleep, appetite and patience.
其实一点点压力是有用的，它能推着我们赶上截止期限。麻烦的是身体连着紧绷好几周——睡眠、胃口和耐心全都会受影响。
Experts suggest small, boring habits: a fixed bedtime, a walk without your phone, and saying no to one thing every week. Boring usually works better than dramatic.
专家给的建议都挺无聊：固定时间睡觉、不带手机出门走一圈、每周拒绝一件事。别小看无聊，它通常比大动作管用。
tips: 放松下来、停止胡思乱想

articles.zh: 蒸桑拿到底对身体好不好
body: In Finland, sitting in a very hot wooden room is part of everyday life. Visitors often wonder whether a sauna is really healthy, or just pleasantly uncomfortable.
在芬兰，坐在一间很热的木头小屋里是日常生活的一部分。外来的人常常搞不懂：桑拿到底是真的养生，还是只是种「舒服的难受」。
Studies suggest that regular sauna use may relax blood vessels and lower blood pressure a little. Much of the benefit, however, may simply come from resting and doing nothing.
研究显示，经常蒸桑拿可能让血管放松，把血压稍微降一点。不过好处里有很大一部分，也许只是因为你终于坐下来什么都不干了。
It is not for everyone. If you have heart problems, are pregnant, or start to feel dizzy, keep the session short and drink water. Comfort matters more than endurance.
但它不适合所有人。有心脏问题、怀孕，或者一进去就头晕的，时间就别太长，记得补水。舒服比硬撑重要。
